pulls.body:
Part of the effort discussed in #35994: replace procedural, field-by-field construction of `COutPoint`, `CTxIn` and `CTxOut` in test code with constructor calls.

This PR covers cases that are context-dependent and need manual changes, independent of a scripted-diff for the trivial bulk:
- `test/util/transaction_utils`: in `BuildSpendingTransaction`, the `scriptWitness` assignment has to be moved after `vin` is replaced, otherwise the witness is dropped.
- `test/util/mining`: in `CreateBlockChain`, the coinbase input's fields were split by the output assignments, with comments that are now kept next to the constructor arguments.
- `sigopcount_tests`: `BuildTxs` has the same witness ordering issue as `BuildSpendingTransaction`.
- `bench/ccoins_caching`: The `scriptSig`s are built with `<<` appends, and the second output was created by `vout.resize(2)` but never assigned, so it is kept as a null `CTxOut{}`.
- `transaction_tests`: `test_Get` builds the same transaction as `bench/ccoins_caching`, with the same `<<` appends and null second output.

**This change is test- and bench-only and does not change the constructed transactions.**

Notes for reviewers:
- `CTxIn` has no witness constructor argument, so `scriptWitness` is assigned after `vin` is replaced.
- `BuildTxs` is called repeatedly on the same transaction objects. Previously, `resize(1)` kept the existing inputs and only overwrote some of their fields; now they are replaced entirely. The fields that were left untouched by `BuildTxs` are never modified by the test, so the transactions are unchanged.
- The null second output in `ccoins_caching` is copied from `test_Get` in `transaction_tests` and looks like an oversight. It is kept here to avoid behaviour changes.

pulls.title: rest: don't log an error for /spenttxouts on a block without undo data
pulls.body:
`/rest/spenttxouts/<hash>` reads the undo file for every block above genesis. For a block that was stored but never connected (a side branch) or whose undo data was pruned, there is no undo position, so `OpenUndoFile()` fails and `ReadBlockUndo()` writes `OpenUndoFile failed for FlatFilePos(nFile=-1, nPos=0)` to debug.log with `LogError`. The request itself already returns 404, but each unauthenticated request for such a block adds an `[error]` line that looks like disk corruption.

This checks `CheckBlockDataAvailability()` for `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO` before reading, so nothing is logged. Pruning clears `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO`, so pruned blocks are covered too. The response is unchanged.

The new check at the end of `interface_rest.py` requests a stale block and fails on master because of the logged error.

pulls.title: node: batch block file pruning in a single pass over block index
pulls.body:
When starting a node with pruning enabled (e.g. `-prune=550`) on a node with full chain history or pruning many files at once, `FindFilesToPrune` and `FindFilesToPruneManual` previously called `PruneOneBlockFile` once per file.

Because `PruneOneBlockFile` iterated over the entire `m_block_index` for each file, this was an O(M * N) operation (M = files to prune, N = total blocks). When pruning a full chain (~5,770 files and ~972k blocks), this triggered ~5.6 billion iterations and froze the node running on a Pi 5 for ~10 minutes on startup while holding `cs_main`.

This PR replaces `PruneOneBlockFile` with `PruneBlockFiles(const std::set<int>&)`, which collects all candidate files and prunes them in a single O(M + N) pass over `m_block_index` using a compact dynamic `bitfield (std::vector<bool>)`. Also skips entries without block or undo data to avoid unneeded checks and prevent file 0 pruning from dirtying header-only or already-pruned index entries. The new signature is analogous to `UnlinkPrunedFiles({file_number});`.

Benchmarked with ~972k blocks and 5,770 files to prune:
- x86_64 (i7-8665U @ 1.90 GHz): 75.1s -> 14.7ms (~5,100x speedup)
- ARM64 (Raspberry Pi 5): 606.0s -> 26.3ms (>3,500x speedup)

Add unit test `blockmanager_prune_block_files_batch` to verify batch pruning, empty set no-ops, and clean dirty-set behavior. Update caller tests in `blockmanager_tests` and `rescan_tests`.

pulls.title: logging: make trace logging easily usable
pulls.body:
**Problem**: Currently it is difficult to enable `trace` logging. 

The `-loglevel=trace` setting works, but does nothing by default and needs to be combined with `-debug` settings to have an effect.

Additionally, it is not possible to switch between `debug` and `trace` logging at runtime without restarting the node. These problems make `trace` logging less useful than it could be, effectively make existing `trace` logs undiscoverable, and making it not worthwhile to add new tracing.

**Solution**: Fix these issues by allowing the `-loglevel` option to work without an accompanying `-debug` option, and by adding a matching `loglevel` RPC that allows log levels to be configured at runtime.

**Usage examples**:
```bash
bitcoin rpc loglevel                               # See current log levels
bitcoin rpc loglevel trace                         # Set global level to -loglevel=trace
bitcoin rpc loglevel debug                         # Set global level to -loglevel=debug
bitcoin rpc loglevel info                          # Set global level to -loglevel=info
bitcoin rpc loglevel libevent=info                 # Set category level to -loglevel=libevent:info
bitcoin rpc loglevel trace net=debug libevent=info # Set global & category levels to -loglevel=trace,net:debug,libevent:info
```

**Compatibility:** This PR is backwards compatible and doesn't change the `-debug` and `-debugexclude` options (which become synonyms for `-loglevel=debug` and `-loglevel=info`, respectively). The `logging` RPC is also mostly unchanged, except now it validates category names before updating log levels, instead of failing with half-applied changes. Also the `logging` RPC now only toggles between `info` and `debug` levels instead of trying to remember previously assigned levels, which was needlessly confusing.

pulls.title: net: make orphan reconsideration more granular
pulls.body:
We currently concentrate the validation of all the assigned peer’s reconsiderable orphans that are still missing inputs in a single message-processing turn. This ties orphan processing to validation result, and adds latency to processing other peers' messages.

Always process a single reconsiderable orphan per turn instead. This removes the need for an immediate validation result, and shifts the latency from other peers to the assigned peer.

pulls.title: wallet: deprecate replaceable argument from transaction (and psbt) creation (and modification) RPCs
pulls.body:
Fixes #32661.

The `replaceable` argument in several wallet RPC requests
has been marked deprecated and for now users have the
option to use this argument via the `-deprecatedrpc=bip125`
startup option. Affected RPCs are `createrawtransaction`,
`fundrawtransaction`, `createpsbt`, `walletcreatefundedpsbt`,
`send`, `sendtoaddress`, `sendmany`, `sendall`, `bumpfee`,
and `psbtbumpfee`.

This builds upon the existing issue of removing the option for
users to signal replaceability because fullrbf is the default policy
and prevalent in the network (since bitcoin core v28 was released
in late 2024) that makes every transaction replaceable by default,
making this user option unnecessary.
